te: Laws along the beef cattle production and marketing chain studied
se: The meeting studied the laws on managing beef cattle production and marketing, setting a framework to consider the whole chain, from problems and causes to the relevant laws and proposed solutions
it: Laws on beef cattle production and marketing

te: Briefing by the Department of Agricultural Extension, the Cooperative Promotion Department and the farmers' council
se: The meeting considered support for beef cattle farming and heard the Department of Agricultural Extension, the Cooperative Promotion Department and the National Farmers Council. They said there are almost ten thousand beef cattle community enterprises, most with medium potential, which are limited because they are not legal entities and so find it hard to obtain funding. Community enterprises should therefore be strengthened
it: Promoting and supporting beef cattle farming

te: Briefing by farmer funds and the BAAC on funding for beef cattle farmers
se: The meeting considered beef cattle farmers' access to funding and invited representatives of the farmer assistance fund office, the Farmers Assistance Fund administration division and the Bank for Agriculture and Agricultural Cooperatives to explain funding support measures and the development of production structures
it: Access to funding for beef cattle farming

te: Briefing by the OAE on the cost of fattened cattle and the effects of free trade
se: The meeting noted information from the Office of Agricultural Economics that the cost of producing fattened cattle varies by breed, the main costs being breeding stock and concentrate feed, and that at times selling prices fall below cost. It also studied the effects of free trade agreements and financial mechanisms to support Thai beef cattle
it: Situation, production costs and effects of free trade agreements
Financial mechanisms to support Thai beef cattle

te: Key issues: breed improvement to meet market demand, and production technology
se: The meeting considered 2 key study issues. For example, beef cattle breed improvement should start from targets set by market demand. Thailand already has good sires, but its base cows are not yet up to standard, so standards for size and meat quality should be set to serve each market level, and farm management technology, such as artificial insemination, should be used
it: Beef cattle breed improvement and production technology

te: Briefing by the Department of Internal Trade and the Department of Foreign Trade on beef prices
se: The meeting studied beef retail prices, domestic market development and the import and export situation. A representative of the Department of Internal Trade said the price farmers receive for live cattle has kept falling while beef retail prices have stayed level, because midstream costs such as labour, slaughterhouse fees and butchering have not come down
it: Beef prices, the domestic market, and imports and exports

te: Briefing by NSTDA on technology-based traceability systems
se: The meeting noted information on animal identification systems from a representative of the National Science and Technology Development Agency, who presented the example of the traceability system for Thai durian, which uses QR codes to track data from the orchard to the consumer, so that the approach can be considered for beef cattle

te: Briefing by the Department of Livestock Development on animal registration and traceability
se: The meeting invited a representative of the Department of Livestock Development to give information on problems in beef cattle production, the animal identification system, breed development, movement control and traceability. The meeting felt the national animal identification system (NID) should be upgraded to cover every head of cattle, so that there is an accurate database to support trade and exports, and discussed using cattle as collateral for loans
it: Animal registration, breed development and traceability

te: Problems of cattle fatteners heard, and the beef cattle market studied
se: The meeting considered a letter from the Phetchaburi Provincial Farmers Council on problems in cattle fattening. Farmers' representatives said they are affected by imports of beef and offal from abroad, high prices of breeding stock and feed, difficult access to funding and low prices for fattened cattle. The subcommittee will use the proposals in its study of the market, prices, processing and standards for beef cattle
it: Letter on problems in cattle fattening, from the Phetchaburi Provincial Farmers Council
Situation and problems of beef cattle marketing, prices, processing and standards

te: Orders changing positions and appointing subcommittee members noted
se: The meeting noted the orders changing positions and appointing subcommittee members and advisers to the subcommittee, and continued its work under the study framework
it: Orders changing positions and appointing subcommittee members and advisers

te: Meeting 2/2568 · Subcommittee to Study Breed Improvement and Integrated Marketing Strategy Development for Beef Cattle to Increase Competitiveness
Work begins: appointment order noted, and a framework for the integrated beef cattle study set
se: The meeting noted the order appointing the subcommittee, whose duty is to study information, facts, laws and measures on integrated beef cattle breed improvement and marketing strategy, in order to propose to the government ways to increase farmers' competitiveness. It considered a framework for working within the set period, starting with a study of the situation and problems of beef cattle breed improvement
it: Framework and timeframe for the work

te: Meeting 9/2568 · Subcommittee to Study Cooperatives in the Agricultural Sector
Preparing a study visit to agricultural cooperatives in Suphan Buri
se: The meeting prepared the study visit on cooperatives in the agricultural sector in Suphan Buri Province on 17 December 2025, preparing questions on how the cooperatives operate and the support they receive from provincial agencies, in order to gather information on the debt problems of cooperatives and their members for the report
it: Preparations for the cooperative study visit, Suphan Buri Province, 17 December 2025

te: Restoring the royally granted rice mill in Kalasin Province followed up
se: The meeting followed up progress in restoring the operation of the royally granted rice mill in Non Sila Loeng Subdistrict, Khong Chai District, Kalasin Province, which has stopped operating. It invited the Director-General of the Cooperative Promotion Department, a representative of the operating cooperative and the mill restoration working group to explain, and the subcommittee gave recommendations so that the mill can operate again
it: Progress in restoring the operation of the royally granted rice mill, Kalasin Province

te: Proposals to separate cooperative laws by type and to promote household accounts
se: The meeting considered solving the debts of cooperatives and their members, the related laws and regulations, and the related funds. Proposals included separate cooperative laws for each type, to suit how each is managed, promoting supplementary occupations for members, and promoting household accounts to solve debt sustainably
it: Proposals on laws, debt and funds related to cooperatives
